Job Description
The Role
General Motors is seeking passionate, driven individuals to join our Customer Care and Aftersales "CCA", Field Sales Operations Internship Program for Summer 2027. This 12-week, project-based internship offers students the opportunity to learn about the District Manager, Parts and Service "DMPS" role while gaining hands-on experience supporting dealers and contributing to the growth of General Motors’ parts and service business across the United States.
Each intern will be assigned to one of General Motors’ five Sales, Service and Marketing regions: Northeast, Southeast, North Central, South Central, or Western. Throughout the program, interns will learn alongside District Managers and Zone Managers through field visits, dealer interactions, business projects, and mentorship. They will gain insight into how General Motors partners with dealers, supports parts and service growth, and delivers an exceptional customer experience. Midway through the internship, interns will spend time in a Central Office in Warren Michigan to learn how Customer Care and Aftersales teams work with regional field teams and other business functions to support dealers, improve the customer experience, and advance General Motors’ broader business strategy.
The Team
The Customer Care and Aftersales Field Sales Operations team works with General Motors dealers across the United States to help grow their parts and service businesses and deliver an exceptional customer experience. The team connects General Motors’ broader business priorities with the day-to-day needs of dealers and their customers.
Field team members build relationships with dealers, understand local business opportunities, and help put regional strategies and initiatives into action. Central Office teams provide the strategy, analysis, tools, and resources that support dealer success across the regions. Together, these teams collaborate with dealer partners and other business functions to improve performance and strengthen the customer experience.
As an intern, you will learn from and work alongside District Managers, Zone Managers, regional leaders, Central Office partners, and other Customer Care and Aftersales professionals. Your experience will include regional immersion, field travel within your territory, Central Office exposure and travel, mentorship, and a capstone project tied to a real business opportunity.
What You’ll Do
Gather and analyze field-level information with regional and Central Office teams.
Identify trends and key drivers of parts and service performance across national, regional, and local markets.
Develop practical insights and repeatable reporting tools that support field sales effectiveness and dealer growth.
Support regional initiatives, campaigns, and dealer engagement strategies that grow the parts, accessories, and service business.
Participate in field visits and structured shadowing experiences, including planning, dealer meetings, follow-up, and action tracking.
Translate dealer and customer feedback into clear observations and recommendations for the regional team.
Prepare concise updates that communicate project progress, risks, and learnings to leaders and program sponsors.
Complete a capstone project addressing a regional opportunity, from defining the opportunity through analysis and recommendations.
Present project findings and recommendations to regional and Customer Care and Aftersales leaders at the conclusion of the internship.
During the program, you will also:
Gain exposure to General Motors’ regional field structure, dealership operations, and the District Manager, Parts and Service role.
Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to real-world business challenges.
Learn how customer, dealer, and market information informs sales and service strategies.
Build confidence communicating with dealers, regional leaders, and Central Office stakeholders.
Develop resilience, adaptability, and professional judgment while navigating varied dealer needs and market conditions.
Understand how regional priorities connect to broader enterprise strategy.
Explore tools and technologies used in sales operations, performance reporting, and dealer engagement.
Build a professional network across regional and Central Office teams.
Program Experience
This is a full-time, 12-week internship that blends regional immersion, field travel, and Central Office exposure.
The program includes:
Weeks 1–2: Regional onboarding and early field exposure
Weeks 3–4: Field travel with District Managers and Zone Managers
Weeks 5–6: Central Office immersion in Warren, Michigan
Week 7: Wholesale and ACDelco Market Area Manager experience
Weeks 8–9: Additional field travel and regional project work
Weeks 10–12: Capstone completion and regional presentation
Throughout the program, you will participate in regular check-ins with your leader and program sponsors to support your development, address challenges, and shape the internship experience.
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Communications, Supply Chain Management or related field.
Expected graduation between December 2027 and June 2029.
Valid driver’s license.
Available to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the summer internship.
Willingness to travel extensively within your assigned region.
Willingness to travel to the Central Office in Warren, Michigan, for a required two-week immersion during the internship.
Strong analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Comfortable working independently in the field and collaboratively with a team.
Willingness to travel extensively within your assigned region and to Central Office program events.
Preferred Qualifications
Demonstrated leadership through academics, extracurricular activities, prior internships, or community involvement.
Interest in the automotive industry, customer experience, and dealer success.
Interest in a field-based commercial career path, such as District Manager, Parts and Service, or a related role.
Experience working with information, dashboards, or business analytics tools to support decision-making.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt quickly, and take initiative in ambiguous situations.

Job Description
University Student Intern – Hot Gas Path Value Engineering & Project Management
Job Description
This University Student Intern role will be a key contributor within the Product Management function supporting the Pivot to Value (P2V) Hot Gas Path (HGP) Value Engineering team. The Intern will support strategic initiatives focused on improving safety, quality, delivery, cost, and capacity across GE Vernova’s Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path product portfolio, including blades, nozzles, shrouds, and near flow path seal (NFPS) components.
Working alongside Product Managers, Value Engineers, Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Supply Chain, Repair, Quality, and Field Services teams, the Intern will participate in projects that drive value optimization, cost reduction, manufacturability improvements, lifecycle cost reduction, and execution excellence for HGP parts. This role provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience supporting component-level value engineering while learning how engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, repair, and commercial teams collaborate to deliver customer value.
Value Engineering is a practice focused on identifying and implementing solutions that optimize product value through improved design, manufacturing efficiency, repairability, sourcing strategies, quality enhancement, and cost reduction. The Intern will support these efforts through project coordination, cost analysis, data management, business case support, and engineering-focused problem solving across the HGP portfolio.
Roles and Responsibilities
Support Value Engineering initiatives for Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path components, including blades, nozzles, shrouds, and related high-temperature hardware.
Assist Senior Engineers and Value Engineering leaders with project execution related to design optimization, manufacturability, sourcing alternatives, repair strategies, lifecycle cost reduction, and capacity improvement.
Gather and analyze cost, manufacturing, field execution, supplier, repair, quality, and operational data to support business cases, project prioritization, and value capture.
Track schedules, milestones, risks, action items, financials, and value realization metrics across multiple projects using project management tools, dashboards, and reporting systems.
Collaborate with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Quality, Repair, and Field Services teams to identify and implement improvements that reduce cost, cycle time, COPQ, and total lifecycle cost while improving quality, yield, productivity, and delivery performance.
Participate in value engineering workshops, cost-out ideation sessions, continuous improvement events, and gated Value Engineering process activities from idea generation through execution tracking and value realization.
Prepare project reviews, stakeholder updates, executive-level presentations, standard work, process documentation, lessons learned, and best-practice repositories.
Learn and apply Value Engineering methodologies, project management principles, cost optimization practices, and engineering-focused problem solving.
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business, or a related technical discipline.
Sophomore standing or above with at least one academic term remaining following completion of the Co-Op assignment.
Demonstrated academic achievement and interest in engineering, manufacturing, project management, or operations.
Ability to work full-time during the Co-Op assignment period.
Desired Characteristics
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Interest in power generation equipment, gas turbine technology, high-temperature components, manufacturing operations, repair processes, and field services.
Excellent organizational and project coordination abilities.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments while working in a fast-paced environment.
Experience with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, or similar data analysis tools.
Familiarity with project management concepts and methodologies.
Ability to analyze data and present findings in a clear and concise manner.
Demonstrated teamwork and collaboration skills.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality work.
Interest in cost analysis, business case development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, engineering drawings, and industrial equipment is preferred.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies is a plus.
Passion for learning and working alongside experienced engineering and business leaders.
What You Will Gain
Exposure to GE Vernova’s Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path product portfolio, Value Engineering organization, and cross-functional cost-out processes.
Hands-on experience supporting HGP component value engineering, cost-out, manufacturability, repairability, and sourcing improvement projects.
Practical experience with project management, business case development, cost tracking, and value realization across a complex engineering product portfolio.
Opportunity to work directly with Senior Engineers, Product Managers, Manufacturing Leaders, Sourcing, Supply Chain, Repair, Quality, and Field Services teams.
Experience developing business cases and supporting value creation initiatives.
Understanding of how engineering, manufacturing, sourcing, supply chain, repair, and field operations collaborate to optimize product value and deliver customer solutions.
Exposure to continuous improvement, capacity growth, operational excellence, and Value Engineering methodologies within the power generation industry.
This Intern position offers a unique opportunity to develop technical, business, and leadership skills while contributing to meaningful projects that improve Hot Gas Path product value, component cost, manufacturability, repairability, quality, and operational execution.

Our Fab 9 location in Essex Junction, VT  is looking to hire Equipment Engineer Interns who are in pursuit of and have completed their first year in a 4-Year Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering or other relevant discipline to sustain and run the fab floor with primary responsibility of resolving equipment and process issues. Drive continuous improvement efforts in support of throughput improvement, cost reduction, and yield learning.
Define and maintain equipment installation process qualification or installation roadmaps

Design, execute, and analyze experiments to screen and optimize equipment to meet technology (performance, yield, and reliability) and manufacturing (process stability, cost of ownership) targets.

Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements, and programs.

Education – A sophomore at the time of application and actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field through an accredited degree program during the time of internship.

Language Fluency - English (Written & Verbal)
Travel - Up to 10%
Ability to work at least 40 hours per week during the internship.

Prior related internship or co-op experience
Project management skills, i.e., the ability to innovate and execute on solutions that matter; the ability to navigate ambiguity.
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Strong planning & organizational skills
Knowledge of Semiconductor Manufacturing
Knowledge of Statistical Process Control (SPC) and Design of Experiments (DOE)
Ability to work effectively and efficiently with diverse teams, customers, internal and external partners.

Welcome to Haleon. We’re a purpose-driven, world-class consumer company putting everyday health in the hands of millions. In just three years since our launch, we’ve grown, evolved and are now entering an exciting new chapter – one filled with bold ambitions and enormous opportunity.
Our trusted portfolio of brands – including Sensodyne®, Panadol®, Advil®, Voltaren®, Theraflu®, Otrivin®, and Centrum® – lead in resilient and growing categories. What sets us apart is our unique blend of deep human understanding and trusted science.
Now it’s time to fully realise the full potential of our business and our people. We do this through our Win as One strategy. It puts our purpose – to deliver better everyday health with humanity – at the heart of everything we do. It unites us, inspires us, and challenges us to be better every day, driven by our agile, performance-focused culture.
Analytical Chemistry is a pillar of Trusted Science and enables us to put health in more hands.
The R&D Global Analytical Development Team supports innovation and development of new over-the-counter products globally. This important work includes physical and chemical assessment of new products, with a focus on generating robust analytical data to support formulation development and product performance.
As an Analytical Chemistry Co-Op, you will contribute to the evaluation of novel topical and nasal drug products through advanced analytical techniques used throughout the pharmaceutical industry. Students may be assigned to projects focused on rheological characterization of formulations or in vitro release testing (IVRT) supported by liquid chromatography. These techniques play an important role in understanding product performance and supporting the development of safe and effective medicines throughout the product lifecycle.
Rheology, IVRT, and liquid chromatography are widely utilized across the pharmaceutical industry to characterize drug products, understand product behavior and performance, and support regulatory and quality requirements. Through hands-on laboratory experience, you will work alongside scientists to generate meaningful data that supports the development of consumer healthcare products from early-stage development through commercialization.
Key Responsibilities
Handle and analyze semi-solid and solution-based drug products using standard pharmaceutical practices.
Learn and operate specialized analytical instrumentation, which may include rheological, Franz diffusion cell (IVRT), and liquid chromatography systems.
Utilize software tools to characterize formulation properties and analyze experimental data.
Execute laboratory testing to assess physical properties, drug release, and other critical product attributes.
Perform basic statistical analyses to evaluate formulation performance and support data interpretation.
Execute standard laboratory procedures and sample preparation techniques for analytical testing.
Interpret and implement regulatory guidance related to analytical characterization of consumer healthcare products.
Generate, critically analyze, and document data using electronic laboratory notebook practices.
Prepare reports, presentations, and conclusions to communicate scientific findings.
Collaborate with scientists to support method development, evaluation, and validation activities.
Qualifications and Skills
Essential
Chemistry or Pharmaceutical Sciences majors are preferred; other scientific disciplines may be considered if candidates have completed coursework in Analytical Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Spectroscopy, or related laboratory-based sciences.
Candidates should be available to work for the entirety of calendar year and be graduating between December 2027 and May 2028.
Preferred
Creative, curious, and able to independently solve problems.
Strong prioritization and analytical skills.
Personal accountability and a desire to learn while making a meaningful impact.
Experience working effectively and efficiently with others.
A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater is preferred.

This internship requires working at the designated location. Candidates requiring relocation are responsible for arranging and funding their own housing, transportation, and relocation needs.
Candidate must be able to work full-time (40 hours/ week) Monday-Friday ~8am-5pm for 6 months.
Candidate must be authorized to work in the United States and will not require sponsorship in the future. Work authorization documentation will be required during the application process.
The position is based in Richmond, requiring an in-office presence of 4-5 days per week

Freshman: $20.00/hour

About Us
Wellington Management offers comprehensive investment management capabilities that span nearly all segments of the global capital markets. Our investment solutions, tailored to the unique return and risk objectives of institutional clients in more than 60 countries, draw on a robust body of proprietary research and a collaborative culture that encourages independent thought and healthy debate. As a private partnership, we believe our ownership structure fosters a long-term view that aligns our perspectives with those of our clients.
About the Role
Wellington Management is seeking motivated undergraduate students to join our 2027 Technology Summer Internship Program. This 10-week paid internship provides hands-on software engineering experience, mentorship, and exposure to the investment management industry and the technologies that support it.
Technology plays a critical role in enabling Wellington's investment, business, and client teams. Our technologist's partner with teams across the firm to build innovative solutions, improve decision-making, and support the needs of a global investment organization.
Interns will work full-time (40 hours/week) at our Boston headquarters beginning June 2027. Interns are eligible for a housing stipend and a flexible work model that includes four days per week in the office and one remote workday.
Designed for students from a variety of academic backgrounds, this program is intended for candidates with prior experience in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related technical field who want to apply those skills to building practical technology solutions. Interns will have the opportunity to explore career paths in Wellington’s technology organization and do meaningful work alongside experienced professionals.
What You'll Do
As a summer intern, you will work alongside a cohort of fellow interns on a summer-long project focused on building a software solution that addresses a real business challenge at Wellington. Working as part of a project team, you'll gain hands-on experience in software engineering, data analysis, and product-oriented problem solving while developing technical, professional, and leadership skills.
Summer Project Experience
Collaborate with fellow interns to identify, design, build, test and deliver a software application that addresses a real business challenge facing Wellington.
Analyze user needs, gather feedback, and apply creative problem-solving to develop solutions that drive meaningful business impact.
Gain hands-on experience applying software engineering and data analysis skills, including requirements gathering, application design, coding, testing, user feedback, and iterative delivery.
Take ownership of a key project workstream while partnering closely with teammates and stakeholders to achieve shared goals.
Build relationships across the firm through networking, collaboration, and engagement with business and technology professionals.
Present project outcomes, recommendations, and lessons learned to senior leaders at the conclusion of the program.
Work on challenges that evolve each year to reflect changing business priorities, emerging technologies, and opportunities for innovation.
What You'll Gain
Throughout the program, interns will:
Gain exposure to the intersection of technology, business, and investment management within a global asset management firm.
Experience how diverse technology disciplines work together to solve complex business challenges and deliver value for clients and colleagues.
Develop technical, analytical, and professional skills through hands-on experience, mentorship and real-world project work.
Build meaningful relationships with leaders, professionals, and fellow interns across the firm.
Strengthen communication, collaboration, leadership, and problem-solving skills in a supportive and team-oriented way.
Gain confidence presenting ideas, influencing stakeholders and translating complex concepts into actionable recommendations.
Explore potential career paths within technology while developing a deeper understanding of Wellington’s culture and business.
Who Should Apply
We welcome students from a broad range of majors, backgrounds, experiences, and academic disciplines. Candidates should have experience applying technical skills through coursework, internships, research, independent projects, or other hands-on work in software engineering, data analysis, computer science, information systems, or a related field.
We look for:
Current sophomore or junior undergraduate students pursuing a bachelor's degree.
Strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Experience with software engineering, data analysis, or a related technical field, including familiarity with at least one programming language such as Python.
Involvement in campus organizations, leadership activities, volunteer work, or other extracurricular experiences.
Ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment.
No prior finance experience is required.
Curious and adaptable in exploring emerging technologies and AI tools in your work, school, and projects
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.
